name: Double Outlet Right Ventricle with Subaortic or Doubly Committed Ventricular Septal Defect

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic and Cardiac MRI Diagnostic Criteria for DORV with Subaortic or Doubly Committed VSD

criteria.description: Both great arteries arise predominantly from the right ventricle confirmed by imaging
Presence of a subaortic or doubly committed ventricular septal defect adjacent to the semilunar valves
Signs of cyanotic congenital heart disease including central cyanosis and heart murmur
Evidence of left-to-right or bidirectional shunting across the VSD on echocardiography or cardiac catheterization

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Anatomical confirmation of both great arteries arising from the right ventricle plus identification of a subaortic or doubly committed VSD on imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on detailed cardiac imaging including echocardiography and cardiac MRI or catheterization.

pathognomonic.notes: Bluish discoloration of lips and mucous membranes due to hypoxemia

pathognomonic.symptomName: Harsh systolic murmur at left lower sternal border
pathognomonic.notes: Due to turbulent flow across the ventricular septal defect

common.notes: Rapid breathing due to congestive heart failure
Shortness of breath on feeding or activity

occasional.notes: Swelling of lower extremities secondary to heart failure

searchTerms: nerve issues from lack of oxygen

rare.notes: Infective endocarditis due to abnormal cardiac anatomy
Elevated pulmonary artery pressures from chronic shunting

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) in heart failure
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating both great arteries arising from right ventricle and subaortic/doubly committed VSD
Cardiac MRI confirming anatomy and shunt quantification
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and pulmonary vascular markings
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be associated with chromosomal anomalies in some cases

distinguishingFeatures: Overriding aorta rather than both great arteries arising from right ventricle
Pulmonary stenosis with right ventricular outflow tract obstruction
Aorta arises from right ventricle and pulmonary artery from left ventricle
Absence of ventricular septal defect in some cases
Parallel rather than crossed great arteries on imaging

redFlags: Severe central cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Signs of congestive heart failure in neonate
Sudden onset of arrhythmia or syncope
references: Anderson RH, et al. Double outlet right ventricle: anatomy and diagnosis. Heart. 2014;100(10):803-810.
Marelli AJ, et al. Congenital heart disease in the general population: changing prevalence and age distribution. Circulation. 2007;115(2):163-172.
Orphanet: Double outlet right ventricle with subaortic or doubly committed ventricular septal defect (ORPHA:423693)
